findings.what: Each of these sheets is a flat fill of one colour with a torn stencil cut out of it: I labelled the connected regions of exactly #F1ECDF and found six slabs filling 59 to 76 per cent of their own card's bounding box, 260,907 px in all, 5.81 per cent of the frame, and an 80x80 window at (1280,2640) is 99.8 per cent one RGB triple with a Rec.601 luma standard deviation of 0.025 grey levels against a mean of 236.0.
findings.why: The anti-goal names 'a beige rounded rectangle' and a surface that 'reads as an approximation of paper rather than as a photograph of real paper' as a failure of the entire visual concept, and this is a beige fill with a paper-shaped hole punched in it; the same widget renders as real stock elsewhere, so the failure is this module's and not the medium's - the flattest 60px window inside the chat voice row at (1070,1050) in 02_chat.png reads std 1.295, and the flattest inside the Moments card at (1294,2634) reads std 0.0000.

findings.where: the top and bottom torn edges of the voice card at x994-1389 y2554-2733, at column x=1190
findings.what: The deckle is two tear masks butted together along a dead-straight vertical line at the card's exact mid-width: tracing the first pale pixel down each column, the top edge steps 21 px at x=1190 (2549 to 2570) with no other jump over 8 px anywhere along its 396 columns, the bottom edge breaks at the same column, and the left half carries almost no fibre spikes while the right half is dense with them.
findings.why: The anti-goal names 'a tiled repeating texture' as a failure of the visual concept, and a mask laid twice across one sheet with the join showing is that failure made visible; at 500 per cent it reads as a straight scissor cut through the middle of a torn edge, which is the one thing a torn edge cannot contain.

findings.what: The file exempts the photograph's sky in 14_media_viewer.png on the ground that 'the sky's flattest window reads 0.619' and its per-still row reports flattest 0.554 with 0 windows under the floor; measuring the same still myself over 80x80 windows with mean luma above 190 I find 61 windows under 0.5 and one at (160,280) that is 100.0 per cent a single RGB triple, #E3E4E9, standard deviation exactly 0.0000.
findings.why: I agree with the file's verdict - the sky is content inside a rendered photograph, not a surface this build claims is paper, so it is not an anti-goal breach - but the exemption is argued from a number the file's own measurement contradicts, and an exemption that rests on an unreproducible figure is the mechanism by which a real flat fill gets waved through next time.

findings.where: the keys replies_on_the_glass, refusals_on_the_glass and clipped_at_an_edge
findings.what: All three keys are present and all three are null in both files; asked_a_motor_for appears in no region report at all (grep over evidence/logs/*.json returns nothing).
findings.why: refusals_on_the_glass is meant to carry the words the other phone refused in, which is precisely the string most likely to carry product-marketing voice, and the record written so a reader could check those words against the glass is empty - I had to read them off 13_messenger_states.png instead, where they are clean ('it would not go', 'send it again', 'this phone is on an older version and cannot read that').

what_is_working: No product-marketing voice anywhere I could look. I read all 111 display-position strings in logs/strings.json end to end and ran my own regex over all 525 recorded: zero emoji glyphs, zero occurrences of 'user', zero of the app's own name, zero cheer words, zero onboarding voice. The six hits for '!' are all Dart null-assertions inside interpolations (paper.dart:200, calendar_module.dart:184, blob_widgets.dart:387 and three more), not punctuation - no displayed string ends in an exclamation mark.
The app does not name itself even where every app does: logs/pwa.json reads the served manifest's name as 'the other phone'.

The onboarding surfaces, which is where marketing voice normally lives, hold the line. 17_setup_pwa.png reads 'this one, the iphone / two phones, one wire between them, nobody else on it' and 'add it to the home screen / share, then add to home screen. it will not hold on to anything until you do.' 10_first_run.png reads 'first one's yours. / whatever it is. it only goes to one person.' No welcome, no get started, no all set.

Failure copy is plain and takes the blame without apologising: 13_messenger_states.png shows 'it would not go' with 'send it again' under it and 'this phone is on an older version and cannot read that'.

No engagement machinery on the surface built to carry it. 03_us.png at full resolution reads 'RITUALS / 3 kept - 53 times - the last 7 days ago', 'sunday 9 call ... 20 times', 'TO DO / 10 open - 16 done', 'THE SHELF / 2 waiting on you - 6 between you': tallies and dates, no badge, no points, no streak word, no breakage warning, no target to miss. My own scan for unlock/earn/reward/achievement/badge/level up/points/streak/milestone/goal/challenge over all 525 strings returned one hit, 'a milestone' at spine/types.dart:291, not in a display position, and that lens is labelled WHAT HAPPENED on the glass.

Notifications carry no machinery either: logs/reception.json records every body the worker showed as 'wrote something', 'is holding something out', 'said how they are', titled with the person's name, and crops/reception_state.png and reception_replaced.png show them on the glass with no count, no badge and no re-engagement prompt. 05_settings.png offers wake me / quietly / not at all per kind plus a quiet window from 23:00 to 07:00.

No emoji soup and no stock illustration in the emotional layer. Frame 95 of 15_authored_feeling.mp4 is the feeling picker - exactly where an emoji grid would sit - and it is six torn paper chips (WARMTH, ACHE, SHELTER, MISCHIEF, STATIC, SPARKLE) over a grid of rendered objects with lowercase labels: poke, nyeh, catch, pick one, snap, stuck with me. In 07_feeling_landing.mp4 the feelings land as objects that cast shadows on the notes under them (the sprig at frame 300 labelled 'a squeeze' and 'nuzzle', the orange band at frame 370). The objects carry surface rather than being flat shapes: local-detail rms inside the 'hold' form in 01_pulse.png is 11.96 and inside the 'nyeh' sweet 8.55, against 14.76 for a written note's interior.

Outside 04_moments the paper holds up. crops/02_chat_300_hand.png at three hundred per cent shows a deckle with individual fibres standing off it and a lightened halo where the sheet thins; crops/02_chat_300_shadow.png shows a hairline contact shadow under the edge. Across nine of the ten stills the largest contiguous run of a single RGB value is 443 to 1,047 px - 0.01 to 0.02 per cent of frame - and the two other Moments lenses measure 647 and 443 px, so the flat fill is specific to one lens and not the medium.

The folded sheets in the clips are real too: stepping 06_unfolding.mp4 at frames 70, 84, 98, 112 and 140, the flattest 60px window on the unfolding sheet reads std 1.17 to 1.84, the same order as the stills.
crops/dusk_pulse.png carries the whole scene through a second lighting condition - paper to warm cream, desk darker, shadows longer - with no anti-goal drift and no emoji.
verdict: Three of the four anti-goals are met, and met with evidence a reader can check rather than by assertion: I read every display-position string and found no exclamation mark, no 'user', no app name and no cheer; the PWA manifest calls the app 'the other phone'; the rituals surface counts without scoring and the notifications name a person without counting anything; and the feeling picker, which is the natural home of an emoji grid, is a sheet of rendered objects with lowercase labels. The fourth fails, in the place the row says costs double. The six voice-note cards in the WHAT WE SENT lens of 04_moments.png are a flat fill of #F1ECDF with a torn stencil over them - six slabs of one exact colour filling 59 to 76 per cent of their own bounding boxes, 5.81 per cent of the whole frame, an 80x80 window 99.8 per cent one triple at luma std 0.025 - while the identical widget in 02_chat.png measures std 1.295 and every other still in the set tops out at a thousand contiguous pixels of one colour. One of the six additionally shows two tear masks butted along a straight vertical line at its exact mid-width, the top edge stepping 21 px at x=1190 with no other jump above 8 px in 396 columns. I checked scenes/04_moments.json before filing it: the lens settles 2,400 ms plus a 900 ms shot settle, and 04_moments.report.json records all 18 blobs asked for as arrived with none reading and none waiting, so this is the finished render of a voice tile and not a picture taken too early. That is a beige rectangle with a paper-shaped hole in it and a tiled edge on top - both named in the anti-goal as failures of the entire visual concept - and it is what holds this row at 7 against a floor of 9. It is bounded: one lens, one widget, one module, on a build whose paper is otherwise convincing at three hundred per cent, which is why the score is 7 and not lower. The missing artifacts cost this row nothing and their reasons are reasons rather than excuses: 09_two_devices.png and 16_setup_android.png are absent because there is no /dev/kvm, measured rather than assumed (adbd answered after 113 minutes and the framework never came up behind it), and nothing was faked from the PWA - and no Android-only screen could hide an anti-goal the PWA does not also show, since the strings and the material library are one. 15_authored_feeling.mp4 is excluded by the frame check for a repeated frame and a light jump, which is a motion fault and not mine; the file is on disk and I stepped through all 420 frames of it anyway.

not_worth_opening.why: six frames each; I decoded the mp4s myself with OpenCV and built denser labelled contact sheets (21 to 23 frames per clip, every 14th to 28th frame), plus full-resolution pulls of individual frames, which strictly contains what the strips show. Frame counts I decoded match frames.json exactly (286, 421, 639, 300, 420).

logs/reception.json says in the record that this scene is not one of the artifacts. I opened two of the five crops and the log to read the notification wording, which is a string the app displays and therefore mine; the permission-prompt and browser-chrome frames carry no app string.

per-frame build and raster cost and fling simulation traces. Nothing in a frame-timing number can show engagement machinery, emoji, marketing voice or simulated paper; I judged the scroll from the clip's pixels instead.
launch timings, flake rates and a test transcript. None of the four anti-goals is a timing or a pass rate, and the strings the tests assert on are already in strings.json, which I read in full.

69 KB of per-surface bookkeeping for the material library. I took the paper measurements myself off the shipped PNGs, which is the artifact the row is judged on, rather than reading the build's inventory of what it believes it drew.
audio records. There is no audio anti-goal, and I could not hear them in any case.
another reader's conclusions, not evidence. The briefing says to leave them closed and I did not open them.

not_worth_opening.path: the repository source under app/lib and the build history
not_worth_opening.why: out of bounds for this row by the briefing, and the code reading of the strings belongs to the code critic. I judged the strings as logs/strings.json recorded them and as they appear on the glass, and I name its self-declared limit rather than going around it: it read 525 of 3,828 literals in lib, 13.7 per cent, and says it cannot see a sentence assembled from parts at the point of use.
